how: Members recruited hands to begin the figure, sustain slow work, and finish its logo.
Members acknowledged that few participants made work slow and movement difficult.
A member proposed the shared figure in the same utterance that called others to build it.
The start and recruitment call can be one utterance rather than separately observable stages.
A proposed yellow background received a bare assent asking for nothing back.
The visible bare assent answers a design proposal and does not establish the specified mobilisation-call acceptance mechanism.
The call precedes a progress report, but these concepts do not identify which builders the call recruited.
Members expanded the figure into a named subreddit display with a skull and skeleton.
Participants publicly reported how far the work had progressed.
Members translated the design into outline instructions, pixel corrections, a requested grid, and a supplied reference.
A posted template settles design only when participants can stabilise its reference rather than repeatedly changing it.
Builders maintain a usable reference through correction and explicit requests to stop changing it.

statement: Moving live coordination between the host thread and an art-specific chat
how: Complex work prompts a dedicated chat while public threads retain corrections, requests, progress reports, and routes to updated plans.
A single room cannot test the population claim, and local instructions alone establish neither formal leadership nor its absence.
Reported manual placing does not determine whether scripts or spare accounts also operated outside the visible thread.
Members deferred some repairs, reverted overwrites, cleaned stray pixels, and rallied to fix damaged parts.
Upkeep begins when an unfinished part can already be overwritten, so construction and defence may overlap before a completion announcement.
An outside participant reported repairing the art and privately sending the plan to people placing grey pixels.
A neighbour explained an unintended overlap, while an apology attributed other damage to someone missing the agreement.
Repeated repair is visible without a demonstrated subsequent turn to machine placement, whose off-platform use remains unobserved.
Participants negotiated a neighbour's name below the sign and tolerated a sun beam behind their figures.
Members refused expansion that would demolish existing art and apologised for damage despite an agreement.
An apology explicitly recalled the agreement to leave the neighbour's lettering alone, showing a local agreement invoked to support restraint.
Neighbour relations included requests, offers, greetings, and construction help promised in return for moving a name.
An offer to move a neighbouring name was answered with agreement and a promise of construction help.
A participant described two neighbouring groups as allies whose help could be requested during a difficult move.

statement: Relocation requires the work first to have been erased or overrun.
how: A speaker advocated migration because staying risked future total overwrite, making the move preventive rather than contingent on accomplished loss.
Relocation includes pausing maintenance on the old sprites and restarting construction at a destination located against a fixed landmark.
The relocation episode returns to building when a participant reports that the new figure has started at the destination.
Relative numerical weakness accompanies a speaker's explicit choice of migration over the risk of defending current ground.
Earlier overwrites and later neighbour negotiations do not establish that the same neighbouring group caused both or that one prompted the other.
Promised outside assistance must remain distinct from completed assistance when the report itself warns that the promise may not be true.
A member reported contacting an outside administrator about relocation without establishing authority to bind all placers.
An apology for someone missing an agreement does not establish a dispute over anyone's right to make it.
The neighbouring-name agreement and subsequent apology reveal no statement disputing who can commit the room.
A surviving permission request does not establish a granted hosting arrangement or subsequent rule over a guest's work.
Suggested requests for outside help do not establish that maintenance strain caused another room to supply it.
The reported alliance and possible help do not establish that shared maintenance strain caused coalition formation or fulfilled mutual defence.
A participant carried rhythm-game vocabulary into the placing work by describing pixels per musical beat.
Naming a political subreddit does not establish a quarrel carried into this canvas effort from before the event.
A report about another group's planned attack does not identify a prior tie motivating an attack by this room.
A false game-completion claim was challenged and then explicitly explained as a joke.
Creating an art-specific chat establishes a venue choice without demonstrating a host-subreddit posting boundary or regulatory intervention.
A recruitment call and a chat move do not establish that a flood of canvas posts prompted host regulation.
Participants celebrated completed parts, claimed small contributions, thanked makers, and expressed bittersweet surprise at shared completion.
The progress report and later completion announcement support a local build-to-celebration sequence without proving every placer's response.
A post-event participant recorded the claimed survival of the figures in the final screenshot.
An atlas referral supports an invitation toward documentation rather than a completed entry when its coded span contains only a link cue.
A retrospective ending added to an edited opening post cannot be dated from that post's original creation time.
Celebration and documentation references do not establish that the former caused the latter, especially where an ending is an undated edit.

statement: A visible mark bringing a reader into the subreddit
how: A visitor attributes finding the subreddit to the canvas work, establishing one reported discovery without demonstrating lasting membership.

statement: Answering canvas visitors through ordinary game discussion
how: Canvas visitors draw out a game explanation and defensive responses to criticism, returning ordinary conversation to the host room.
Accepting an imperfect skeleton in the final screenshot does not establish a contest over cleaning or preserving a historical version.
Post-event thanks and a documentation referral establish neither continuing organisation nor a decision to repurpose the effort.
A survival record and an atlas referral show no subsequent decision to continue the temporary effort.
An individual's separate void participation and a report about another group's attack do not establish a collective attack by this room.
A visitor's music provocation and the reply to it do not establish a contest with a rival canvas room.
Recruitment and separate individual void participation do not establish that the room's call turned into a rival attack.
Refusing destructive expansion is visible without a coded attack call shown to have elicited the refusal.
Neighbour accommodation cannot be attributed to an unobserved attack call.
Reported overwrites and defensive visitor talk do not establish an attack by this room causing a rival-room contest.
